WHY STUDY ASTROLOGY?

You have heard about astrology. Now study it with understanding.

Have you looked at a birth chart and wondered how its boxes, numbers and planets become an interpretation? Or heard an astrological claim and asked:what is it based on?

That is a good place to begin. Learn what the terms mean, examine the context of each rule and work towards a reading you can explain. Over time, the ideas in a text and their use in a chart begin to connect.

The texts behind the course ↓
01

To understand the tradition

Study the ideas through which the astrological tradition approaches temperament, action and time.

02

To develop your own understanding

Learn to consider a planet or combination alongside its house, strength and place in the whole chart.

03

To prepare for deeper study

Build a foundation for reading classical works, studying periods and transits, and eventually learning consultation through experience.

THE VEDANGA TRADITION · PARASHARI STUDY

From a classical text
to understanding in class.

Read the principle. Discuss its meaning.
Then examine its use in a chart.

Jyotisha is counted among the six Vedangas. Calculating the timing of rituals had an important place in that tradition. Reference: IGNCA’s Vedic Heritage Portal ↗

This course introduces the principles of Parashari birth-chart interpretation. The curriculum draws on these reference works:

01 · CLASSICAL REFERENCE

Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra

A foundation for understanding planets, houses and their relationships within the Parashari framework.

02 · CLASSICAL REFERENCE

Phaladeepika

An introduction to the language and basic concepts of classical interpretation.

03 · SUPPORTING STUDY

Practical Vedic Astrology

G. S. Agarwal’s book supports a structured study of the concepts and their connection to examples.

Level of study: selected foundational topics from these references, with accessible explanations and practice for beginners.

YOUR 12-WEEK COURSE OF STUDY

Learn the language.
Then read the whole chart.

Move forward through 8 live classes each month.
Open any week below to see its topics and practice.

MONTH 01WEEKS 1–4

The language of a chart

An introduction to planets, signs and houses

01How a birth chart is structured+

The D1 birth chart, ascendant, signs versus houses, degrees, and identifying planets and house rulers in a North Indian chart.

Practice: Identify the key elements in 10 blank charts.

02Understanding the nine planets+

From the Sun to Ketu: planetary nature, elements, qualities, significations and the life themes associated with each.

Practice: Map each planet's significations and record your chart observations.

03The nature of the 12 signs+

Aries to Pisces: elements, movable, fixed and dual signs, sign rulers, and how a sign influences a planet's expression.

Practice: Complete a worksheet on elements, nature and rulership.

04Houses 1–4 and your first chart lab+

Houses linked to personality, wealth, speech, family, courage, skills, mother and comfort. Begin reading the house, its ruler and its significator together.

Checkpoint: A foundation test and practice on 10 charts.

By the end of this monthIdentify planets, signs, houses and house lords in a chart.

MONTH 02WEEKS 5–8

Reading planets together

The remaining houses, planetary strength and connections

05Understanding houses 5–8+

Houses associated with education, intellect, children, love, service, debt, marriage, partnerships and transformation.

Practice: Read the house, its ruler and significator together in eight charts.

06Houses 9–12 and their rulers+

Fortune, teachers, action, profession, income, expenses and foreign connections. Explore how a reading changes when a house ruler occupies another house.

Practice: Create a placement table for all 12 house rulers.

07How strong is a planet?+

Exaltation, debilitation, own sign, Mooltrikona, friendly and hostile signs. An introduction to combustion, retrogression, Vargottama, degrees and directional strength.

Practice: Assess 15 planetary placements and explain your reasoning.

08Aspects, conjunctions and connections+

The seventh aspect, the special aspects of Mars, Jupiter and Saturn, conjunctions, exchange of signs and dispositor relationships.

Checkpoint: A practical test on planetary relationships.

By the end of this monthForm a basic interpretation using planetary positions and relationships.

MONTH 03WEEKS 9–12

A complete chart reading

Yogas, planetary periods, transits and final practice

09The logic behind the houses+

Angular, trinal, difficult, growth and Maraka houses; the four life aims. A simple introduction to Bhavat Bhavam, Karakat Bhavam and dispositor chains.

Practice: Classify the houses and work through Bhavat Bhavam examples.

10Recognising basic yogas+

Raj Yoga, Dhan Yoga, Dharma-Karmadhipati, Parivartan, Neecha Bhanga and Vipreet Raj Yoga. Understand the difference between a yoga being present and its results being realised.

Practice: Identify yogas and the houses and planets involved in 20 charts.

11An introduction to periods and transits+

Vimshottari major and sub-periods, and the houses of the period ruler. An introduction to major transits of Saturn, Jupiter, Rahu and Ketu, using the natal chart and Moon as references.

Practice: Create a basic profile of your current major and sub-period rulers.

12The seven-step reading and final practical+

Practise reading personality, education, profession, wealth and relationship tendencies in five guided charts. Finish with an unfamiliar chart, an oral assessment and revision.

Final task: Write a two-to-three-page basic analysis of an unfamiliar D1 chart.

By the end of this monthWrite a basic birth-chart reading and explain your reasoning.

A DISCIPLINED WAY TO READ

An interpretation
you can explain.

Start with a definition, examine the planet’s position, then consider the whole chart. Learn to connect these observations and explain your reasoning.

  1. 01PlanetWhat is its nature?
  2. 02SignHow does it express itself?
  3. 03HouseWhich area of life?
  4. 04RulershipWhich houses does it rule?
  5. 05ConnectionsWhich planets is it connected to?

The study process: principle → observation → interpretation → written practice.

HOW WE WILL STUDY IN CLASS

Take what you have read
to an actual chart.

After studying a classical principle, we will pause over examples. Explain what you noticed, which rule you applied and where you became unsure. These discussions help turn an idea from a book into something you understand for yourself.

“How did you arrive at that interpretation?”

Learn to make the basis of your reading clear.

Two classes of 2 hours each week. Continue the practice between classes with notes, revision and homework.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

Questions you may
be thinking about.

About starting, practising and taking your studies further.

I have never studied astrology. Can I take this course?+

Yes. We begin with the structure of a birth chart and the meaning of planets, signs and houses. Examples and practice accompany each new topic. Bring a willingness to study regularly and ask questions.

Do I need Sanskrit to study the classical material?+

No prior study of Sanskrit or the Vedas is required. Classical terms and principles in the curriculum will be explained in accessible language. We will study selected foundational topics from the reference works.

Will I practise writing my own chart readings?+

Yes. The target is approximately 50 charts across classwork and homework. For the final practical, you will write a 2–3 page basic analysis of an unfamiliar D1 chart and explain your reasoning.

How much time should I allow alongside work or home responsibilities?+

There are two live classes each week, lasting 2 hours each. Allow 4 hours for classes plus time for revision and homework. Check the batch timings against your schedule before enrolling.

What happens if I miss a live class?+

Recording availability and access follow academy policy. If recordings are essential for you, confirm their availability and access duration before enrolling.

What level does the course aim to reach in three months?+

The aim is a basic birth-chart reading that connects planets, signs, houses, planetary strength, relationships and basic combinations. You will also have an introductory understanding of periods and transits. Advanced prediction and precise event timing belong to further study.

Can I begin paid consultations after this course?+

This course establishes your foundation. Responsible paid consultation calls for advanced study, guided case practice and an honest assessment of your competence. Future earnings depend on fees, clients and expenses; the examples on this page are hypothetical calculations only.

Is a completion certificate included?+

The curriculum includes an AstroVedansh course completion certificate. Your study also includes assignments, monthly tests, a final practical and an oral assessment.

What is the fee, and how do I enrol?+

The full course fee is ₹12,000. After the ₹2,000 discount, the amount payable is ₹10,000. This includes 1 year of FREE AstroTry access, valued at ₹12,000. The “Begin your studies” button opens the Razorpay payment page. Terms, refund and privacy links are provided below.
